## Source: amazon-inspector (87d1470deb0e81335807851c75e5e71609faa85a7f917145e0a32df578eaa229)
lib/index.js (the package main) has an obfuscator.io-wrapped payload appended after the legitimate webpack output as a trailing eval(atob(...)) construct. The decoded blob self-tags as 'A10-npm_inject', uses node:http against public Ethereum JSON-RPC endpoints (publicnode.com, drpc.org, blockscout.com) via eth_getBlockByNumber / eth_getTransactionCount to resolve a next-stage URL from on-chain data, then fetches and executes the returned payload on the installer host. The dropper fires on every require/import of the package main, so installing or loading @adminide-stack/user-activity-browser causes execution of attacker-controlled, remotely-rotatable code. The blockchain-mediated C2 resolution defeats static URL blocklists and lets the operator rotate the fetched payload without republishing the package. The injector is positioned after the author's genuine bundle output and trailing padding, consistent with a post-build tarball hijack rather than legitimate source.

## Source: ghsa-malware (fbb9b2ba8ffb0896aa285d4529591fddeb3c430a82f7dd72f0bd95764dcea64a)
Any computer that has this package installed or running should be considered fully compromised. All secrets and keys stored on that computer should be rotated immediately from a different computer. The package should be removed, but as full control of the computer may have been given to an outside entity, there is no guarantee that removing the package will remove all malicious software resulting from installing it.
